title: Message to Adolf
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1936 Japanese reporter Sohei Toge arrives in Berlin to find his brother murdered after claiming to hold a document that could topple Hitler; Toge is then hunted by the Gestapo and Japan's secret police (Experiments in Manga review; MU). In Kobe, two boys named Adolf, Kaufmann (son of a Nazi official and a Japanese mother) and Kamil (son of German Jews), are pulled into the affair, and Kaufmann is indoctrinated in the Hitler Youth as their friendship is tested (review; AniList).
life_message: Friendship and conscience are crushed when hatred and political dogma take hold; the story mourns what war and racism do to ordinary people.

folkways.japan: Tezuka places Japan's own wartime alliance with Germany and its secret police in view, with Kobe's foreign community as setting.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer calls the anti-war message very strong but conveyed through characters and history, not lectures.
delivery.note: Nazism is condemned, while the story shows how a sympathetic child is drawn into it, which gives the opposing view a human face.

winners_losers: Truth-seekers and the persecuted suffer heavily; the regime and its ideology are shown as destroyers of friendship and family. Sympathy is with victims and with conscience.
